How often should I brush my cat?

For a short-haired cat, once or twice a week is usually enough to remove loose hair and cut down on hairballs. Long-haired breeds do better with a short daily session, which also keeps mats from forming. If you notice bald patches or the skin looks irritated while brushing, mention it to your vet.

My dog has been drinking a lot more water than usual. Should I be worried?

A sudden increase in thirst is worth paying attention to, especially if it lasts more than a day or two or comes with more frequent urination. Warm weather, more exercise, or a switch to dry food can explain it, but it can also point to something that needs testing. I would note when it started and book a check-up so your vet can rule out the medical causes.

What is the difference between preventive and reactive care?

Preventive care is the routine you keep up while your pet is well: check-ups, vaccines, parasite control, balanced food, and dental care. Reactive care is what happens after a problem appears, such as treating an injury or an illness. Both matter, but preventive care is usually cheaper and less stressful for your pet because it catches issues early.
